speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the appearance and distribution of your skin lesions, as they may be linked to your wrist pain and fever. Also, have you noticed any joint swelling or morning stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, and Lyme serology. REQUEST IMAGES: Skin lesions of left wrist and knee. Have you experienced any tick bites while camping in Minnesota?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC shows WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; ESR and CRP are not in the provided data; Lyme serology is not in the provided data. Skin lesions of left wrist and knee were not imaged in the provided data. The patient has not reported experiencing tick bites while camping in Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI). The elevated WBC, recent sexually active history, and migratory polyarthralgia (knee then wrist) are classic for DGI, even in the absence of reported tick bites or positive Lyme serology. Skin lesions in this context are typically sterile, pustular, or petechial.
